name: C11_SURVIVOR_PAIR_RELATION_REPRESENTATION
fixed_context: One ordered type pair (T,T'), one stored 111 state (p,m,n), one post-Lemma10 descendant P'.

definitions.Sigma: Sigma(v)={C in CC : v is complete to C}
definitions.A: {y in Y'(T) intersect N(Y0') : ym is a nonedge}
definitions.B: {y' in Y'(T') intersect N(Y0') : y'm is an edge}
definitions.R_C11: {(y,y') in A x B : yy' is a nonedge and Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') is nonempty}

target_claims: For every v in Y', adjacency of v is constant on each connected component C of G[Y0'].
N(y) intersect N(y') intersect Y0' is nonempty iff Sigma(y) intersect Sigma(y') is nonempty.
After the exact z-fiber quotient, the graph-discoverable survivor family is exactly R_C11.
A common-component identity is a certificate only; it carries no additional answer-relevant semantic coordinate beyond (y,y').
No equivalence between distinct survivor pairs is claimed.
proof_basis: Descendant axiom (iv): no vertex outside Y0' union X0' is mixed on an edge of Y0'.
Vertices y,y' lie in Y', hence outside Y0' union X0'.
Adjacency therefore propagates unchanged along every path inside a Y0' component.
Acceptability semantics is defined on y,y', their lists, and extension colors; common z is selected only afterward as proof witness.
forbidden: identify distinct pairs with equal Sigma signatures
claim equal extension projections from equal Sigma signatures
